q: Implement `Readonly2<T, K>` (readonly only for chosen keys), Mutable, PickByType/OmitByType.
mcqAngle: Pick the correct Mutable definition using `-readonly`.

q: Implement Diff or Flatten type challenges.
mcqAngle: Predict `Diff<{a: 1; b: 2}, {a: 1}>`.

q: Use key remapping in mapped types (`as` clause) to build types like `Getters<T>` that produce `getName`, `getAge`.

evidence.note: Guide aimed at Meta, Snap, Airbnb, Shopify style loops

mcqAngle: Predict the keys produced by remapping each key K with `as` to the template literal get${Capitalize<K & string>}.

q: Generate typed event-handler names (e.g. `onThemeChanged`) from an object's keys using template literal and mapped types.
mcqAngle: Pick the mapped type that produces exactly the handler names expected.

q: Type a React component whose props are mutually exclusive (for example `href` or `onClick`, never both).
mcqAngle: Pick the union-with-never props type that rejects both being passed.

q: Build a type-safe design-system variant map that fails type-checking when a variant is missing, without widening literals.
mcqAngle: Pick the declaration using `satisfies Record<Variant, string>`.

q: Implement a type-safe event emitter where an event map ties each event name to its payload type.

evidence.note: Guide aimed at Meta, Snap, Airbnb, Shopify style loops

mcqAngle: Pick the `on<K extends keyof Events>` signature that rejects a wrong payload.

q: Implement a typed `Promise.all` (runtime polyfill and/or the type that maps a tuple of promises to a tuple of results).
mcqAngle: Predict the result type of `promiseAll([Promise.resolve(1), "a"] as const)`.

q: How does TypeScript decide type compatibility (assignability) between two types?
mcqAngle: Predict whether `{a: string; b: number}` is assignable to `{a: string}` (yes, via variable).

q: What are branded (opaque) types and how do they simulate nominal typing, e.g. UserId vs OrderId?
mcqAngle: Pick the branded type that prevents passing an OrderId where a UserId is required.

q: What is the difference between declaration merging and module augmentation? What are the risks of global augmentation?

evidence.note: Guide aimed at Meta, Snap, Airbnb, Shopify style loops

mcqAngle: Pick the correct `declare module "lib" { ... }` block to add a field to a library type.

q: What are assertion functions (`asserts x is T`) and how do they differ from `is` type predicates?
mcqAngle: Predict the type of x on the line after calling an asserts function.

q: How does module resolution work, and what is the difference between CommonJS and ESNext module targets?
mcqAngle: Pick the moduleResolution setting suited to a bundler-based frontend.

q: What is the polymorphic `this` type and how does it help with method chaining in subclasses?
mcqAngle: Predict the return type of a chained call on a subclass when the base method returns `this`.

q: What are recursive types? Give an example such as a JSON value type.
mcqAngle: Pick the valid recursive JSON type alias.

q: How do mixins work in TypeScript?
mcqAngle: Pick the correct mixin function signature using a constructor type.

q: How do you describe the type of a class created inside a function and returned (typeof Class, InstanceType)?
mcqAngle: Pick the type that represents instances of the returned class: InstanceType<ReturnType<typeof make>>.

q: How do you manage complex shared types across many files in a large TypeScript codebase?
mcqAngle: Pick a sound practice (single source of truth, derive types from schemas/constants).

q: How do you keep type safety at the boundary with external services or REST APIs (runtime validation, generated types)?
mcqAngle: Pick the true statement: static types do not validate network data; a runtime schema check is needed.

q: How does the TypeScript compiler work at a high level (parse, bind, check, emit)?
mcqAngle: Pick the compiler phase that reports type errors (checker).

q: Do you use `any` in interview or production code? How do you treat it in a strict codebase?

evidence.note: Vercel guide: loose typing / any is flagged as a negative signal

mcqAngle: Pick the best practice: prefer unknown with narrowing; treat any as tracked, time-boxed debt.

q: Explain variance (covariance, contravariance, bivariance) and how it affects function parameter compatibility and strictFunctionTypes.
mcqAngle: Predict whether `(x: Animal) => void` is assignable to `(x: Dog) => void` under strictFunctionTypes (yes) and the reverse (no).

q: What are the compiler performance costs of complex recursive types, and how do you fix "type instantiation is excessively deep"?
mcqAngle: Pick the change most likely to reduce type-check time (simplify recursion, use interfaces over large intersections).

q: Implement `UnionToIntersection<U>`.
mcqAngle: Predict `UnionToIntersection<{a: 1} | {b: 2}>`.

q: Implement an `Equal<A, B>` type and write type-level tests (Expect<Equal<...>>) for your utility types.
mcqAngle: Pick the Equal implementation that distinguishes `any` from `string`.

q: Implement string-casing types: CamelCase, SnakeCase, KebabCase.
mcqAngle: Predict `KebabCase<"FooBarBaz">`.

q: Implement an `ObjectPaths<O>` type that yields all dot-separated key paths of a nested object.
mcqAngle: Predict the union of paths for a two-level object.

q: Implement the Chainable Options type challenge (a builder whose final `get()` returns the accumulated object type).
mcqAngle: Predict the type returned after chaining two option calls.

q: Implement type-level Permutation or String-to-Union challenges.
mcqAngle: Predict `Permutation<"A" | "B">`.

q: Implement a typed `curry` function whose curried calls keep the original parameter types.
mcqAngle: Pick the type signature that correctly curries a 3-argument function.

q: Design the type layer of a shared component library or design system so invalid prop combinations and variants are impossible and refactors stay safe.
mcqAngle: Pick the API design that turns a runtime prop check into a compile-time error.
